newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour Party increases opinion poll lead.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour Party increases opinion poll lead.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party has taken advantage of confusion within the ruling Conservatives to notch up its largest lead in opinion polls since March, the Times reported on Thursday.

A MORI poll for the newspaper said support for Labour had risen by four points to 56 percent while the Conservatives had slipped one point to 28 percent. The minority Liberal Democrats had dropped two points to 12 percent.

The newspaper said the ruling Conservatives, facing a general election by next May, had not impressed voters by setting out a programme for the next year and then hastily agreeing with the opposition to add new laws on curbing paedophiles and obsessive stalkers.
The Conservatives are also split over new anti-gun laws in the wake of the massacre of 16 children and their teacher by a lone gunman at Dunblane in Scotland earlier this year.
Those polled said they disapproved of Prime Minister John Major by a two-to-one margin and were unhappy with the government by a margin of four-to-one.
MORI interviewed 1,747 people face-to-face at 161 sampling points across Britain between October 25 and 28.
